_provenance.notes: Alaska ocean conditions are tracked through multiple indices: Eastern Bering Sea cold pool extent (warm/cold years), Gulf of Alaska sea surface temperature anomaly, and the Integrated Ecosystem Assessment (IEA). These ocean conditions drive fish production more strongly than fishing effort for most Alaska species.

annual_ocean_conditions.description: Annual Alaska ocean condition summary — EBS and GOA indicators that affect fisheries productivity

NOAA PMEL. 2008 cold year — excellent cold pool. Crab recruitment.

NOAA PMEL. 'THE BLOB' BEGINS — 2014-2016. Most extreme marine heatwave ever recorded in NE Pacific. SST anomaly +4-5°C in some areas.
NOAA PMEL. The Blob peak + strong El Nino. Toxic algal blooms. Unusual marine mammal mortality events. Seabird die-offs.
NOAA PMEL. Blob dissipating but warm conditions persist. Salmon production severely impacted.
NOAA PMEL. Partial recovery of cool conditions in EBS.
NOAA PMEL. WARM YEAR yet RECORD BB SALMON. Demonstrates complexity — Sockeye from 2014-2015 brood (pre-Blob) drove the record. Pollock shifted north.
NOAA PMEL. Record low cold pool — almost no cold water on EBS shelf. Snow crab cannot find cold habitat. Mass crab mortality begins.
NOAA PMEL. Partial cold pool recovery. La Nina develops.
NOAA PMEL. La Nina — EBS cold pool strong. Excellent conditions for 2024 salmon returns.
NOAA PMEL. Back-to-back La Nina. Excellent cold pool. Cold pool salmon + record BB returns.
NOAA PMEL. El Nino developing. Conditions moderating.
